sources.title: The Economist: choosing a limited chart palette
sources.finding: The team describes dark and light blue as recurring colors, a small working palette, and highlighting a main series when many series compete.
sources.transfer: Use one recognizable signature color repeatedly, with two companions and a quiet neutral.

sources.title: BBC Visual and Data Journalism: R graphics cookbook
sources.finding: The public cookbook separates its reusable chart theme from explicitly assigned data colors. Examples use blue #1380A1 and other deliberate color assignments.
sources.transfer: Keep typography and framing fixed while changing named color roles. The cookbook is a 2019 public reference, not a claim about every current BBC graphic.

sources.title: ONS: using colours in charts
sources.finding: The palette includes ocean blue #206095, spring green #A8BD3A and beetroot #871A5B. Guidance favors few categories, consistent mappings, and gray context plus a highlighted series.
sources.transfer: Separate an everyday three-color core from an extended palette. Many categories should not automatically mean many equally prominent colors.

sources.title: Datawrapper: colors in data-vis style guides
sources.finding: The guide distinguishes categories, accents, neutral grays, and sequential/diverging scales. Its discussion with the Financial Times explains how a tinted background constrains usable lightness and neutrals.
sources.transfer: Specify a complete system of roles and test colors on the actual cream background, not isolated white swatches.

sources.title: Nature: preparing figures, our specifications
sources.finding: The research-figure guide asks for accessible colors, standard sans-serif fonts such as Helvetica, and dark legend text. It also has its own rules for ticks, grids, patterns and final text size.
sources.transfer: Use the current style as a lab identity, then apply journal-specific output settings at submission. A familiar journal name does not define one universal author-figure palette.

sources.title: ACS Inclusivity Style Guide: data visualization
sources.finding: ACS recommends considering color-vision deficiency and grayscale, matching color-scale type to data, and combining color with direct labels or symbols.
sources.transfer: Use redundant markers and line patterns, and keep categorical identity separate from numerical magnitude.

sources.title: Fabio Crameri: Scientific colour maps
sources.finding: The Scientific colour maps project develops ordered, perceptually controlled scales for quantitative data, including color-vision and grayscale considerations.
sources.transfer: Treat continuous scales as a separate engineering problem. The custom ramps here are prototypes, not replacements for validated scientific maps in demanding measurements.

sources.title: Les Couleurs: Le Corbusier color system
sources.finding: The architectural system contains 63 colors in two collections. It organizes solid colors and graduated shades, and uses color keyboards to explore combinations.
sources.transfer: Borrow the relationship of muted mineral hues, warm neutrals and a few stronger accents. No official swatch set or color codes were reproduced.

sources.title: Albers Foundation: Interaction of Color
sources.finding: Albers's teaching examines how neighboring colors and context change perceived color through practical visual exercises.
sources.transfer: Judge every palette in thin curves, large fills and actual plots on the approved background. This informs the method, not a borrowed Albers palette.

sources.title: Albers Foundation: In Thread and On Paper
sources.finding: The exhibition documents movement between woven textiles, prints and functional design, including cotton samples and wool works.
sources.transfer: Use material and dye associations as creative prompts for P2 and P3. The proposed hex values are new selections, not measured colors from these works.

sources.title: Martian Press: ink colors
sources.finding: The studio works with a finite ink library. It explains that largely transparent inks, layering and paper affect the resulting color; digital swatches are approximations.
sources.transfer: Borrow the limited-ink discipline for P5. Avoid fluorescence, paper texture and overprint effects in quantitative marks; none of its ink palette is copied wholesale.

sources.title: W3C: understanding non-text contrast
sources.finding: The guidance uses a 3:1 contrast criterion for meaningful graphical elements against adjacent colors and notes that thin anti-aliased marks can appear fainter.
sources.transfer: Check opaque series against cream at 3:1 as a screening target. This is not a claim that every complete figure is WCAG compliant.

sources.title: Bjorn Ottosson: Oklab color space
sources.finding: Oklab represents lightness and two chromatic coordinates and supports perceptual color interpolation.
sources.transfer: Build prototype ramps with controlled lightness, then inspect them and test for monotonic luminance after conversion to sRGB.

sources.title: Machado et al. matrices in Colorspacious
sources.finding: This implementation distributes the 2009 Machado, Oliveira and Fernandes simulation matrices over a range of severities.
sources.transfer: Use severity-100 protan, deutan and tritan matrices on linear RGB, plus luminance grayscale. Simulations are screening aids, not guarantees of accessibility.

sources.title: Nature Reviews: figure and illustration guide
sources.finding: For commissioned explanatory illustrations, Nature organizes its house palette into accent colors and neutral context, with an extended palette for grouping and exceptions for scientific conventions.
sources.transfer: Borrow the hierarchy of focus versus context. Distinguish this editorial illustration system from the research-figure specifications; neither is a palette to clone.

sources.title: Okabe and Ito: Color Universal Design
sources.finding: The authors propose blue, sky blue, bluish green, vermilion, orange, yellow and reddish purple with black, and recommend direct labeling and redundant shape/line coding.
sources.transfer: Use this as a functional reference. Our muted material palettes serve identity and require their own checks; they do not inherit the accessibility of another palette.
